item.title: Possible Error
item.content:encoded:
SCP-106-J appears to host and serve based on desire, not hunger. SCP-106-J will collect multiple visitors during a hosting event, keeping many "fed" in the pocket dimension for extended periods of time. SCP-106-J has no determinable limit to the number of patio chairs and paper plates it can provide.

Shouldn't that be cookout dimension?

item.title: Re: One thing I noticed...
item.content:encoded:
One of the things I picked up on when analysing the original SCP-106 in preparation for this was an almost gratuitous use of "terms in quotes" there (sometimes working to ominous effect, but sometimes… not so much (which I thought was a bit funny in itself)).

So in turn, I peppered them into this piece - perhaps gratuitously. Some of them may be subversions of lines from the original article, some of them may be that line of thinking extending into the rest of the writing.

I will give some thought as to whether all of them necessarily contribute to a gag or punchline, or maybe could stand to be replaced with more typical/clinical wording. Thank you for your comment!

item.title: One thing I noticed...
item.content:encoded: There are a lot of "quotes" that get used in various ways, and sometimes it's just to be more colloquial, but sometimes it's not clear on whether you're actually trying to quote someone. This one's doing fine, but maybe something to give some consideration to for improvement down the road. Look at each of those quoted passages and decide what it's really doing and contributing, and if it could be done in a way that doesn't use a source of uncertainty like quotes.

The upvote I gave has absolutely nothing to do with the fact that I am very hungry right now, nor the multiple deep breaths I gave through my nostrils while reading this due to my weakened resolve.

+1 for the barbecue grill dad
